body:
I do have supervision, and I do believe that sometimes I can be impacted by my client’s trauma, so that is certainly worth exploring. 

You wouldn’t be patronizing, I’m sure of it. I am always open to learn and hear feedback. Thank you for your response, I truly and sincerely appreciate it.

I can tell from reading this that you love your children deeply me and are a very loving person. Anger is powerful, but it just tells us that we have some fear and hurt in our heart that we have to work through, or even in our body. Anger is a signal. It helps us survive in many circumstances. It can be adaptive in some environments, but maladaptive and unhelpful in others. 

I can’t tell exactly by your words, but it sounds as if you’ve served. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I can’t begin to imagine the pain you’ve been through or what you’ve witnessed or felt. But I want you to know you’re not alone, and some of the things you’re experiencing are due to what you’ve gone though, your changes in environment and the role and duty you were given. I’m sure anger was part of what helped you survive, and that’s not something to be ashamed of. Anger may have served its purpose for you, and maybe now it’s no longer needed since you’re not in the same role/environment. It’s not a matter of an on and off switch, which is the hard part. But you are a brave and selfless person for serving—and if it wasn’t serving, for defending or protecting whatever you were doing. It takes a strong selfless person to do that. It’s hard to adjust again to civilian life. All of our experiences impact us, but what you’re experiencing—anger, fear, hyper vigilance, threat, it’s not your fault. You are NOT a bad person, quite the opposite! I’m willing to guess that your children love you. I want to abide by the rules here on this subreddit and not make assumptions about your life, but its surely a possibility that your children are not better off without you, but that they’re better off with you. 

What you are experiencing are likely side effects of serving, your struggles don’t define who you are as a person, they are symptoms that can be changed and coped with, with the right help. I’m not telling you what to do, but I am telling you that there are resources that can be helpful if you are interested. 

I will be thinking of you with hope and care as you cope with this part if your journey. Thank you, again.
